corrections.was: A diff of seven changed files. A Scope violation is changing something the brief said not to touch. This brief said, do not edit the shader, the player script or the existing tests. Two files outside it changed, eight lines in all, so check git diff against the brief. The file list is illustrative. For example, you ask an agent to add a pause menu, and it also edits the enemy's patrol script. Even if the game still works, that edit is a scope violation.

corrections.why: The slide defines a scope violation as changing something the brief said not to touch ('A change to a file it ruled out'), but the example's brief never ruled the patrol script out, so it described unrequested extra work (closer to the glossary's scope creep) rather than a true instance.
